basis: Congenital malposition of the great arteries is a structural cardiovascular defect.
Glycosylation disorder defined by developmental disability and seizures; cerebellar atrophy in 2/2. Hypotonia and impaired pursuit do not establish separate muscle or eye damage.
Syrinx formation directly affects the spinal cord.
Reflex epilepsy with seizures triggered by hot water.
Malignant tumour arising in the orbit; skeletal muscle differentiation alone does not establish a separate musculoskeletal site.
Atherosclerotic disease directly affects arteries; downstream organ diseases are not universal and are separately diagnosed.
Eosinophilia 11/11; dermatitis 4/4; colonic eosinophilia 1/1 plus food allergy 11/11 supports gut disease. Renal and hepatic damage prevalence uncertain; four-axis cap.
Cardiac pump failure defines the disease; congestion, edema and pulmonary rales alone do not establish lasting damage to other organs.
Squamous cell carcinoma involving the lacrimal gland, part of the ocular axis.
Congenital structural defect of the oral palate; the mouth belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Inherited muscular chloride channel dysfunction affects skeletal muscle; a neuromuscular classification alone does not imply nerve damage.
Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss; no additional organ disease is established.
Granular cell tumour arising in the heart; tumour location determines the organ label.
Definition specifies hereditary amyloidosis with lung parenchymal deposition; ancestry identifies an inborn metabolic disorder.
Umbrella disorder of myocardium; cardiac muscle belongs to the cardiovascular axis.
Defined by skeletal and connective tissue abnormalities, including arachnodactyly, mandibular hypoplasia and joint laxity.
Necrosis directly destroys bone; insufficient blood supply alone does not establish a separate vascular disorder.
Skeletal dysplasia with vertebral and metaphyseal abnormalities in 80-99%; supplied phenotypes remain within the skeletal axis.
Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia is a cardiac electrical disorder.
Distal myopathy directly affects skeletal muscle, particularly thumb and handgrip muscles.
Localized plasma-cell neoplasm arising in chest-wall bone or soft tissue. Plasma-cell lineage supports haematologic labeling; the lymphoma parent alone is insufficient for an immune label.
Delayed toxic-anoxic brain injury after carbon monoxide poisoning defines this specific concept.
Congenital limb dysostosis involving radial deficiency and tibial hypoplasia.
Umbrella skeletal dysplasia; neurologic, hearing and skin abnormalities of selected subtypes do not apply across most patients.
Inherited haptocorrin deficiency alters cobalamin transport and is usually clinically benign; common anemia or neurologic damage is not established.
